evidence_records.Full citation: Abramson, Corey M., Tara Prendergast, Zhuofan Li, and Daniel Dohan. 2025. Qualitative Research in an Era of AI: A Pragmatic Approach to Data Analysis, Workflow, and Computation. arXiv:2509.12503v5; accepted/forthcoming in Annual Review of Sociology 52 (2026). OSF version DOI: 10.31235/osf.io/7bsgy_v4.
evidence_records.Title: Qualitative Research in an Era of AI: A Pragmatic Approach to Data Analysis, Workflow, and Computation
evidence_records.Authors: Corey M. Abramson; Tara Prendergast; Zhuofan Li; Daniel Dohan
evidence_records.Venue: arXiv preprint; accepted/forthcoming in Annual Review of Sociology 52 (2026)
evidence_records.Publication type: methodological review/guidance with illustrative computational-ethnography workflow
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: accepted/forthcoming; inspected preprint, not final version of record
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v5 posted 2025-09-15 and updated 2025-11-12; SocArXiv/OSF versions are the same family; latest OSF v4. Count once.
evidence_records.DOI: 10.31235/osf.io/7bsgy_v4 (OSF version; journal DOI not yet assigned)
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: OpenAlex: 1 for OSF work and 0 for arXiv record, checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: DISCERN and prior Abramson/Li computational-ethnography work supply some performance claims; no independent current LLM evaluation
evidence_records.Research objective: Offer a pragmatic typology—streamlining, scaling, hybrid work, sociology of computation, and rejection—and illustrate it using DISCERN.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: pragmatic methodological review and computational ethnography workflow
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Conceptual synthesis plus an illustrative longitudinal health-sociology workflow; no formal current-paper evaluation of LLM-generated codes or themes.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid; human theory/method leads, computational tools index, retrieve, and scale stable categories
evidence_records.Domain: older adults, dementia, care partners, and health sociology
evidence_records.Dataset name: DISCERN, a five-year NIH project across three U.S. states
evidence_records.Number of documents: 119 interviews plus more than 300 day-long site visits; exact analyzable-file count not reported
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: large longitudinal fieldwork corpus; exact words/pages not reported
evidence_records.Language: not fully reported; fieldworkers preserve original language and are fluent where required
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: highly sensitive health and participant data
evidence_records.Model family: regex/dictionaries; BERT/RoBERTa/Gemma-2-2B embeddings or local classifiers in described/related workflows; Claude/GPT/Gemini only for manuscript editing
evidence_records.Exact model/version: not adequately reported; no commercial model received study data
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Commercial models limited to language/citation/error editing; qualitative-analysis prompts not applicable/reported.
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: local fine-tuned classifiers described; exact training configuration absent
evidence_records.Agent roles: machines index, retrieve, classify stable categories, and assist pattern discovery; humans interpret
evidence_records.Human role: Primary analysts develop nuanced codes, audit labels, examine disconfirming evidence, and maintain reflexive interpretation.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: source-linked paragraphs/passages and indexed qualitative materials
evidence_records.Generated outputs: indexes, codes/classifiers, memos, embeddings, network and pattern maps
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Stable paragraph IDs, positional metadata, and links back to raw context provide strong procedural provenance.
evidence_records.Baselines: No current-paper formal baseline; manual workflow and prior published work are discussed.
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: None clearly attributable to the current DISCERN evaluation; F1 around .80 is mentioned from prior/related work.
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Weekly review, memoing, disconfirming-case analysis, and reflexive meetings; not a formal comparative evaluation.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: research team; count and expertise by task incompletely reported
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Krippendorff α around .80 is mentioned from prior/related work, not clearly the present case.
evidence_records.Principal results: Human-machine agreement around .80, less than one-third manual time, and “months” saved are not cleanly separated from prior work and are not controlled current-paper estimates.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Qualitative time-saving claims only; no measured cost/compute.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: IRB-governed restricted data, vetted transcription, anonymization/pseudonyms, separated identifiers, secure REDCap/Box/wiki/Git, local models, and no commercial study-data transfer; protocol/consent wording absent.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Teaching/code/templates repository https://github.com/Computational-Ethnography-Lab/teaching, version dated 2025-11-01; original data unavailable under IRB.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Methods and theory must precede tools; small samples may not benefit; local models and documentation still require expertise.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Current-versus-prior evaluation provenance is ambiguous; exact models/configurations and controlled comparisons are absent; commercial tools were used during manuscript production.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Related Abramson/Li computational-ethnography work supplies some metrics; do not treat those figures as an independent evaluation here.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong design guidance on stable source IDs, local processing, negative/minority cases, version logs, and limiting automation to stable/indexical tasks.

evidence_records.Full citation: Zhang, Yan, Haoqi Li, Ramtin Tabatabaei, and Wafa Johal. 2025. ROSAnnotator: A Web Application for ROSBag Data Analysis in Human-Robot Interaction. 2025 20th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction, 1099–1103. https://doi.org/10.1109/HRI61500.2025.10974254.
evidence_records.Title: ROSAnnotator: A Web Application for ROSBag Data Analysis in Human-Robot Interaction
evidence_records.Authors: Yan Zhang; Haoqi Li; Ramtin Tabatabaei; Wafa Johal
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv:2501.07051v1 posted 2025-01-13; VOR published 2025-03-04. One family.
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: arXiv/VOR ROSAnnotator family; no duplicate system report located
evidence_records.Research objective: Provide an accessible web application for synchronized ROSBag exploration, annotation, transcription, and LLM-assisted coding.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Engineering implementation/demo supporting manual and automated segment coding; no empirical validity or usability study.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: supports deductive codebooks and free-text/hybrid annotation
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: potentially high for audio/video HRI recordings
evidence_records.Model family: OpenAI multimodal/API models and configurable Hugging Face access
evidence_records.Exact model/version: not reported, including transcription and multimodal snapshots
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Default and user-modifiable prompts; complete defaults/configuration not adequately documented in the paper.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single-model calls inside a web application
evidence_records.Agent roles: transcription, code assignment, and multimodal-segment interpretation
evidence_records.Human role: Uploads codebook, initiates operations, and may inspect/edit output; verification is not mandatory.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: codes, annotation tiers, transcripts, occurrence/frequency/duration/latency statistics, and CSV
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Annotations remain tied to synchronized ROSBag intervals.
evidence_records.Principal results: Functional capability only; no evidence of coding accuracy, thematic validity, usability, or stability.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Face frames can be removed locally before external video transfer; audio transcription remains external and voice/body/location/transcript/contextual identifiers remain exposed. Redaction may remove analytically important nonverbal context.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: https://github.com/CHRI-Lab/ROSAnnotator; Docker image roughly 20 GB; no benchmark data/output archive
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Automatic annotation is not robust for nuanced HRI; commercial cost; external-audio privacy; built-ins focus on audio/video topics.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: No exact model/configuration, empirical validation, mandatory review, or redaction-effect evaluation.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Useful provenance/infrastructure example, but it must be classified as unvalidated rather than evidence that automated coding works.

evidence_records.Full citation: Sakib, Fardin Ahsan, Ziwei Zhu, Karen Trister Grace, Meliha Yetisgen, and Ozlem Uzuner. 2025. Spurious Correlations and Beyond: Understanding and Mitigating Shortcut Learning in SDOH Extraction with Large Language Models. arXiv:2506.00134v1.
evidence_records.Title: Spurious Correlations and Beyond: Understanding and Mitigating Shortcut Learning in SDOH Extraction with Large Language Models
evidence_records.Authors: Fardin Ahsan Sakib; Ziwei Zhu; Karen Trister Grace; Meliha Yetisgen; Ozlem Uzuner
evidence_records.Publication history notes: v1 submitted 2025-05-30; no later VOR located
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: SHAC/MIMIC benchmark family; not a duplicate qualitative-analysis paper
evidence_records.Research objective: Identify and mitigate shortcut learning in drug-status extraction from social-history notes.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: SDOH information extraction with shortcut analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Fixed-label span/status classification with subgroup false-positive rates and trigger-deletion experiments.
evidence_records.Domain: clinical NLP / social determinants of health
evidence_records.Dataset name: SHAC/MIMIC-III social-history note sections with demographics
evidence_records.Number of documents: 4,405 deidentified sections reported; wording is ambiguous whether this is all SHAC or the MIMIC subset
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Llama-3.1-70B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-Med42-70B, Qwen-72B; checkpoints/inference stack incomplete
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: zero-shot, three-example ICL, chain-of-thought, shortcut warning, and up to eight examples; prompts in appendix
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: Llama-3.1-8B LoRA SFT, rank 64, dropout .1, learning rate 2e-4, batch 4, five epochs, FP16
evidence_records.Human role: inherited reference annotations only; no current human-in-loop interpretation
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: social-history note section and drug-status mention
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Predictions link to note sections/triggers; no qualitative source-audit interface.
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: false-positive rate, primarily for none/unknown, stratified by cues and gender
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: SHAC annotators not characterized in this paper
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive rates only; no uncertainty intervals or tests
evidence_records.Principal results: Llama-70B zero-shot false-positive rates were 66.21% for alcohol-positive, 61.11% smoking-positive, and 73.26% both; chain-of-thought reduced them to 33.79%, 25.93%, and 34.88%. Llama-8B SFT reduced the both-cue FPR from 81.40% to 40.70%. Trigger deletion reduced but did not eliminate errors; gender effects varied.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: LoRA training about three hours on two A100s; inference around 100 GPU-hours on two A100s
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Controlled deidentified data on secure university systems under DUAs/IRB processes; exact protocol IDs absent; authors discuss stigma risk.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: No code/data release; SHAC controlled; prompts and hyperparameters partial.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One corpus, open models only, causal mechanism unresolved, generative setting only, and incomplete mitigations.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Trigger deletion is not a matched causal intervention; subgroup denominators absent; FPR-only hides false negatives; binary gender/site/documentation confounding; mitigation may overfit discovered shortcuts.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong adjacent rationale for subgroup audits, matched counterfactuals, denominators/CIs, multiple metrics, and speaker/participant-cue checks.

evidence_records.Full citation: De Paoli, Stefano, and Alex Fawzi. 2025. TALLMesh: A Simple Application for Performing Thematic Analysis with Large Language Models. arXiv:2504.13892v1.
evidence_records.Title: TALLMesh: A Simple Application for Performing Thematic Analysis with Large Language Models
evidence_records.Publication history notes: v1 submitted 2025-04-05; no archival VOR located
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: Tool implements De Paoli’s earlier 2024 workflow; distinct software artifact, not an independent empirical validation.
evidence_records.Research objective: Create a no-code Streamlit application implementing an LLM thematic-analysis workflow.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Sequential per-document code generation, LLM code deduplication, theme grouping, and a second pass forcing unassigned-code allocation; tool description without outcome validation.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: nominally inductive; optional prompts/codebooks make it hybrid
evidence_records.Number of participants: informal Abertay user testing mentioned; n not reported
evidence_records.Exact model/version: defaults mention GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini; snapshots absent
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: none; DSPy reducer proposed as future work
evidence_records.Agent roles: open coder, code reducer/deduplicator, theme grouper, and forced assigner of unassigned codes
evidence_records.Human role: Configures project/prompts and may inspect/edit; review is afforded but not mandatory.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: code-description-quote CSV, accumulated codebook, themes, visualizations, unique/total-code ratio
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Quotes retained at code stage; theme-level outputs can lose quote/source links.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: none; determinism at zero temperature/top-p is asserted but not tested
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: unique-to-total-code ratio presented as thematic saturation; not validated
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: think-aloud/Miro feedback for interface changes only
evidence_records.Principal results: Functional workflow/interface description only; no coding/theme quality, stability, or comparative result.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Generic advice to check institutional requirements and use Azure/GDPR-compatible deployments; direct OpenAI risks not evaluated.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Documentation/training needed, reducer needs improvement, and open models/broader testing are future work.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Forced theme assignment suppresses unassigned/negative cases; deduplication and saturation ratio unvalidated; dissemination to roughly 100 scholars is not evaluation.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Representative end-to-end architecture; motivates source-linked themes, negative/unassigned states, reducer validation, stability tests, and defensible stopping criteria.

evidence_records.Full citation: Borchers, Conrad, Bahar Shahrokhian, Francesco Balzan, Elham Tajik, Sreecharan Sankaranarayanan, and Sebastian Simon. 2026. Temperature and Persona Shape LLM Agent Consensus With Minimal Accuracy Gains in Qualitative Coding. Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Educational Data Mining, 280–292. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21039879.
evidence_records.Title: Temperature and Persona Shape LLM Agent Consensus With Minimal Accuracy Gains in Qualitative Coding
evidence_records.Authors: Conrad Borchers; Bahar Shahrokhian; Francesco Balzan; Elham Tajik; Sreecharan Sankaranarayanan; Sebastian Simon
evidence_records.Venue: Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Educational Data Mining, pages 280–292
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv:2507.11198v1 posted 2025-07-15, v2 2026-05-10; EDM 2026 VOR preferred. Count once.
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: OpenAlex: 2 for arXiv and 0 for new VOR, checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: 2025 arXiv/2026 EDM family; reuses Barany et al. educational dialogue dataset/reference coding
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether same-model multi-agent deliberation improves coding accuracy and how temperature/persona affect consensus.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Fixed eight-code binary multilabel classification with same-model deliberation; identifying this with thematic analysis is methodologically debatable.
evidence_records.Dataset name: 579 dialogue segments from three transcripts derived from four prior 60-minute sessions
evidence_records.Number of documents: three session transcripts used; four existed in the source study, with one exclusion unexplained
evidence_records.Document length: source sessions approximately 60 minutes; segment lengths not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: minors’ educational dialogue; verbatim data restricted
evidence_records.Model family: Llama, OpenHermes, WizardLM, Phi, Mistral, and DeepSeek
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Llama-3.2-3B, OpenHermes-V2-7B, WizardLM-2-7B, Phi-3-14B, Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506, DeepSeek-R1-32B via Ollama; several tags/checkpoints incomplete
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Full utterance, eight-code codebook, and conversation history; balanced/bold/empathetic personas; up to two critique rounds; one schema-failure re-prompt.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: two same-model coders plus critique; neutral consensus agent resolves residual disagreement
evidence_records.Agent roles: coder A, coder B, critic/deliberator, and fallback consensus agent
evidence_records.Human role: No deployment-time intervention; humans supply adjudicated reference labels and inspect selected deliberation traces.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: eight binary labels, consensus categories, CSV, and deliberation traces
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Dialogue and deliberation traces retained; final labels link to utterances.
evidence_records.Baselines: neutral single-agent control and adjudicated human labels
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: six models × three temperatures × six persona pairings; no explicit stochastic replicates/seeds
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: percent agreement against human labels and consensus-type counts
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Inherited trained double-coded/adjudicated reference plus qualitative analysis of selected agent conversations.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: source annotators plus two current qualitative trace coders
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Source described only as high; current text conflicts between independent double coding and 75 nonoverlapping cases, so no defensible current IRR.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: GLMM with random utterance/code effects, odds ratios/95% CIs, and 432 exploratory paired contrasts with BH adjustment
evidence_records.Principal results: Final/single agreement: DeepSeek 90.0/89.9; Llama 81.6/85.5; Mistral 89.3/89.7; OpenHermes 84.9/85.8; Phi 89.5/89.6; Wizard 85.6/87.2. Only 5/432 contrasts favored MAS, all one OpenHermes subset; 65 favored single agents. Higher temperature often delayed/reduced consensus; traces contained contradictions, hallucinated facts, and invented codes.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: About two hours on an M1 for some experiments; DeepSeek about 60 seconds/datapoint on an A100; total compute/cost absent and MAS adds calls.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: No IRB, consent, deidentification, or child-data statement despite minors’ transcripts.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One dataset/mature codebook, deductive only, same-model agents, persona dependence, and no cross-model teams.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reported 77,273 decisions do not reconcile with full factorial 6×18×579×8=500,256; exclusions/denominator unexplained. Raw agreement is prevalence-sensitive; no F1, sensitivity, balanced accuracy, or code-prevalence analysis.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Barany et al. dataset/reference-coding dependency; one arXiv/EDM family
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: High-value negative finding that same-model consensus is not accuracy; require denominator reconciliation, prevalence-aware metrics, plural humans, privacy reporting, and trace audits.

evidence_records.Full citation: Rodriguez, Joshua, Om Sanan, Guillermo Vizarreta-Luna, and Steven A. Conrad. 2026. Text Chunking in Human-AI Teaming of Document Classification for Urban Systems Management Using Large Language Models. IET Smart Cities 8(1). https://doi.org/10.1049/smc2.70023.
evidence_records.Title: Text Chunking in Human-AI Teaming of Document Classification for Urban Systems Management Using Large Language Models
evidence_records.Authors: Joshua Rodriguez; Om Sanan; Guillermo Vizarreta-Luna; Steven A. Conrad
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv:2504.00274v1 posted 2025-03-31 under a shorter title; 2026 VOR is preferred. One family.
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: OpenAlex: 1 for arXiv and 0 for VOR, checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Research objective: Determine whether chunking improves reliable document classification in an urban-system literature review.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Repeated 17-dimension binary classification of ten scientific papers.
evidence_records.Dataset name: ten public scientific papers and 17 expert-derived dimensions
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1-mini; snapshots not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: One dimension at a time, presence/absence plus two supporting pieces of evidence; fresh/reset call per prompt.
evidence_records.Human role: Three nonexperts independently code; majority becomes reference.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: document × dimension; chunking uses nonoverlapping 500-word chunks and document-level OR aggregation
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Evidence requested but not evaluated; label-centric analysis.
evidence_records.Baselines: human majority, whole-document versus chunked strategies, and three models
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: 15 iterations per configuration; seeds/settings not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: internal percent agreement/mode; accuracy, precision, recall versus majority; Fleiss κ
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: three nonexpert coders; no domain-expert gold adjudication
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney, and Wilcoxon tests; multiple-comparison control not reported
evidence_records.Principal results: Whole/chunk accuracy: GPT-4o 74.12/87.65; mini 77.65/84.12; o1 72.35/87.06. Recall rose with chunking. Internal percent agreement rose while within-model κ often fell due to prevalence. Adding GPT-4o as a fourth rater reduced human κ .434→.407; mini produced .437.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: No measured time/cost despite efficiency framing.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Public papers; no human-subject corpus concern.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Small document sample and rapidly changing models.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: OR aggregation confounds chunk count/document length; 86% positive prevalence inflates agreement/accuracy and negative performance is weak; nonexpert reference; ten papers are pseudoreplicated across dimensions/runs; parser was developed/tested on same outputs; κ>.4 is incorrectly called statistical significance.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Useful chunking/stability case; require prevalence-aware metrics, independent labels, unit-matched aggregation, parser validation, and corrected inference.

evidence_records.Full citation: King, Jennifer, Kevin Klyman, Emily Capstick, Tiffany Saade, and Victoria Hsieh. 2025. User Privacy and Large Language Models: An Analysis of Frontier Developers’ Privacy Policies. Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society 8(2): 1465–1477. https://doi.org/10.1609/aies.v8i2.36646.
evidence_records.Title: User Privacy and Large Language Models: An Analysis of Frontier Developers’ Privacy Policies
evidence_records.Authors: Jennifer King; Kevin Klyman; Emily Capstick; Tiffany Saade; Victoria Hsieh
evidence_records.Venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society 8(2): 1465–1477
evidence_records.Research objective: Compare user-privacy policies of six major frontier-model developers.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Human-only coded comparison of policy documents.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid: inductive categories informed by CCPA and AI-specific concepts
evidence_records.Dataset name: 28 policies/subpolicies/FAQs for Amazon Nova, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Meta AI, Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI ChatGPT
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public text; subject concerns sensitive user data
evidence_records.Generated outputs: yes/no/not-specified matrix for collection, use, training, retention, children, and related practices
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Source/reference URLs and access dates supplied.
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Coding divided among team members; each portion reviewed by another.
evidence_records.Principal results: Policies are fragmented/inconsistent, with default-training and potentially indefinite-retention risks. Table treatment of Amazon as not specified appears inconsistent with the blanket prose claim that all six train on chats by default.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Public-document study with strong substantive ethical analysis.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Exact sources/access dates, but no codebook, coded matrix repository, or archived snapshots.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Six U.S.-focused firms, heterogeneous business models, incomplete subpolicies/model cards, and point-in-time analysis.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Policies changed during the study; moving pages undermine reproducibility; some aggregate prose overstates table evidence.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Record service tier, settings, policy date, opt-out/training terms, DPA, retention, and processing geography; do not infer confidentiality from model name.

evidence_records.Full citation: Relins, Sam, Daniel Birks, and Charlie Lloyd. 2025. Using Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models to Identify Indicators of Vulnerability in Police Incident Narratives. Journal of Quantitative Criminology 41(4): 647–684. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10940-025-09611-z.
evidence_records.Title: Using Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models to Identify Indicators of Vulnerability in Police Incident Narratives
evidence_records.Authors: Sam Relins; Daniel Birks; Charlie Lloyd
evidence_records.Research objective: Identify mental ill health, substance misuse, alcohol dependence, and homelessness in police narratives.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: scalable qualitative coding using instruction-tuned LLMs
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Four-label ordinal/binary classification with repeated inference, consensus, and evidence extraction.
evidence_records.Dataset name: Boston Police Department FIO narratives, June 2015–December 2023
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: public PDDL-derived records with OSF release
evidence_records.Number of documents: 32,218 unique narratives after deduplication/minimum-length filter; 4,000 model sample; 500-case human/GPT-4o evaluation subset
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: high: police contact, vulnerability, race, sex, health, housing, and substance use
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Llama nominally 8B/70B and GPT-4o; snapshots absent; paper inconsistently labels Llama sizes 7B/80B elsewhere
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Verbatim codebook, chain-of-thought/evidence quotation, iteratively refined custom prompt, and up to three reparsing attempts.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: repeated single-model inference with majority consensus
evidence_records.Human role: Three authors create codebook; two nonexpert annotators label evaluation data; team adjudicates.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: positive/inconclusive/negative status, evidence, entropy, and consensus
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Evidence quotations tied to narratives; public release redacted.
evidence_records.Baselines: two Llama scales/prompts, GPT-4o, and adjudicated human labels
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: ten labels per Llama narrative; seed/decoding settings not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: ordinal MSE; collapsed precision/recall/F1; confusion matrices; entropy; consensus calibration
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 500 enriched narratives × four vulnerabilities independently labeled then adjudicated
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two nonexpert annotators plus author adjudicators
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: 10,000-bootstrap CIs; counterfactual GLMM with random narrative effects, average marginal effects, Holm correction
evidence_records.Principal results: Custom-8B/GPT-4o F1: mental health .58/.70; homelessness .75/.71; substance .67/.81; alcohol .68/.72. Unanimous-negative precision generally 95–100% over roughly half to two-thirds of narratives. Counterfactual race/sex effects were usually small but nonzero, including GPT-4o Black alcohol −2.81 percentage points and male +1.99.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Weeks/months reduction claimed without measured labor/cost; GPT-4o sample restricted by API cost.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Institution deemed public secondary data not requiring review; records redacted; representational/privacy risk remains high.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One jurisdiction, uncertain generalization, prompt/model dependence.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Evaluation set purposively enriched using tested Custom-70B predictions; no population estimates; nonexpert gold/no IRR; inconclusive collapsed positive; exact models absent; counterfactual edits unvalidated; consensus can stabilize systematic bias.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Important repeated-inference/entropy/counterfactual case; require independent sampling, expert references, matched perturbations, prevalence metrics, and site/officer/boilerplate confound checks.

evidence_records.Full citation: Shanwetter Levit, Neta, and Mor Saban. 2025. When Investigator Meets Large Language Models: A Qualitative Analysis of Cancer Patient Decision-Making Journeys. npj Digital Medicine 8: 336. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-025-01747-3.
evidence_records.Title: When Investigator Meets Large Language Models: A Qualitative Analysis of Cancer Patient Decision-Making Journeys
evidence_records.Research objective: Compare investigator and LLM interpretations of cancer-patient decision-making journeys.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: qualitative thematic analysis with zero-shot LLM comparison
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Human constant-comparative analysis versus per-transcript LLM theme extraction and unexplained corpus-level synthesis; prompts were refined after early quotation failures.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: human analysis inductive; LLM nominally zero-shot inductive
evidence_records.Number of participants: 33 (22 women, 11 men; mean age 56.78, SD 17, range 28–83)
evidence_records.Language: Likely Hebrew because Ivrit.AI transcription was used, but transcript/input language and translation are not reported.
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: highly sensitive cancer and personal decision data
evidence_records.Exact model/version: ChatGPT-4o and noncanonical “Gemini Advance Pro1.5”; no snapshots/dates/routes/settings
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Each anonymized transcript prompted for main themes and two quotations; early paraphrase/misattribution prompted several refinements/interventions.
evidence_records.Agent roles: per-transcript theme/quotation extractor and corpus-level synthesizer
evidence_records.Human role: Lead trained analyst performs full analysis; second researcher reviews framework; humans inspect/correct final quotations.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: Human five-theme framework, ChatGPT six themes, Gemini three themes, and representative quotations.
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Requested quotations, but early misattribution/paraphrase and no shareable transcripts make provenance unauditable.
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Author comparison of conceptual overlap and quotation checking.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: lead trained oncology qualitative researcher and second reviewer
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Cohen κ=.85 claimed for human work, but unit/subset/independence/calculation missing; “reviewed framework” may not justify κ.
evidence_records.Principal results: Human analysis emphasized emotional coping, trust, support, information/decisions, and quality of life. ChatGPT emphasized emotional/physical impacts, providers, internet/information, family, timeline, and autonomy; Gemini produced emotional meaning, physical/side effects, and second-opinion themes. Authors judge humans deeper and LLMs more logistical; some Gemini quotations weaken construct coherence.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: “Weeks” human versus “days” LLM plus checking; no measured hours/cost.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Tel Aviv IRB 0008350-4, informed consent, withdrawal rights, anonymization; no disclosure of consent for proprietary transfer, API retention, DPA, or cross-border processing.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Transcripts unavailable; protocols/prompts reportedly on request; no code/output archive.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Zero-shot variability, fabrication, no cross-analysis prompting, recall bias, and limited diversity.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Language/translation omitted; no blinding; interviewer familiarity advantages humans; iterative human corpus analysis is not task-matched to vague per-transcript LLM process; no participant validation; “zero-shot” conflicts with corrective iteration.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Require task alignment, model/version and multilingual reporting, source verification, participant/domain-expert validation, and explicit API consent/governance.

evidence_records.Full citation: Zhang, He, Chuhao Wu, Jingyi Xie, Yao Lyu, Jie Cai, and John M. Carroll. 2025. Harnessing the Power of AI in Qualitative Research: Exploring, Using and Redesigning ChatGPT. Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 4: 100144. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2025.100144.
evidence_records.Title: Harnessing the Power of AI in Qualitative Research: Exploring, Using and Redesigning ChatGPT
evidence_records.Authors: He Zhang; Chuhao Wu; Jingyi Xie; Yao Lyu; Jie Cai; John M. Carroll
evidence_records.Venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 4: 100144
evidence_records.Publication history notes: Earlier arXiv:2309.10771, titled Redefining Qualitative Analysis in the AI Era, v1 2023-09-19/v3 2024-05-28; journal VOR May 2025. One renamed family.
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: arXiv 2309.10771 and 2025 journal VOR are one renamed family
evidence_records.Research objective: Determine how prompt design affects ChatGPT thematic analysis and researcher attitudes, and develop a prompt framework.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: reflexive thematic analysis plus participatory prompt redesign
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Exploratory think-aloud/coaching sessions: participants self-prompted up to five times, then researchers advised iterative refinement until satisfaction; recordings underwent human RTA.
evidence_records.Dataset name: 17 session recordings/transcripts plus one shared remote-work focus-group transcript
evidence_records.Number of documents: 17 session records and one task transcript
evidence_records.Number of participants: 17 total: four pilot and 13 formal; 12 women/5 men; ages 20–32; formal sample mostly doctoral researchers
evidence_records.Document length: pilot sessions 1–1.5 hours; formal durations not reported
evidence_records.Language: ChatGPT interactions English; research-interview language not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: participant recordings potentially sensitive; task-transcript provenance/sensitivity unknown
evidence_records.Exact model/version: ChatGPT/GPT-3.5; snapshot/date absent; informal GPT-4 check undocumented
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Variable participant prompts plus coached refinements: background, process/method, input/output format, role, prioritization, traceability, and praise.
evidence_records.Human role: Prompts, judges, revises, and is expected to double-check; researchers coach participants.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: codes, themes, quotations, tables, rationales, and prompt framework
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Prompts encourage excerpts/participant source; self-generated rationales are incorrectly treated as transparency/interpretability.
evidence_records.Baselines: participants’ initial versus coached prompts, without controlled order/counterbalancing/blinding
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: up to five initial attempts plus variable refinements; no seeds
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: subjective participant satisfaction, trust, and attitude change
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: 13 formal participants; researcher team codes session data
evidence_records.Principal results: Participants reported improved perceived transparency/usability and shifted from skepticism toward acceptance; no objective efficacy result.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: University IRB approval, consent, and US$10 compensation; no protocol ID or commercial-data-transfer discussion.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: No data, complete interaction logs, prompts, code, or model snapshot.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One corpus, limited diversity, roughly one-hour exposure, coding focus, and evolving models.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Coached order/demand effects; iterate-until-satisfaction; “significant” wording without tests; many users novice/junior; trust conflated with validity; task-corpus provenance absent.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Useful prompting/human-role framework, but trust can rise without validated accuracy; separate usability/trust from validity.

evidence_records.Full citation: Chen, John, Alexandros Lotsos, Grace Wang, Lexie Zhao, Bruce Sherin, Uri Wilensky, and Michael S. Horn. 2025. Processes Matter: How ML/GAI Approaches Could Support Open Qualitative Coding of Online Discourse Datasets. CSCL 2025 Proceedings, 415–418. https://doi.org/10.22318/cscl2025.114185.
evidence_records.Title: Processes Matter: How ML/GAI Approaches Could Support Open Qualitative Coding of Online Discourse Datasets
evidence_records.Authors: John Chen; Alexandros Lotsos; Grace Wang; Lexie Zhao; Bruce Sherin; Uri Wilensky; Michael S. Horn
evidence_records.Publication history notes: Conference paper and longer arXiv:2504.02887v1 (2025-04-02) are one family.
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: Reuses TA-1334/Chen et al. 2024 Prompts Matter 127-message corpus and codebooks; distinct contribution-analysis paper, not independent replication; code-merging line precedes 2026 Findings paper.
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate whether and how machine open-coding processes contribute grounded, useful insights beyond human coders.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Secondary comparison of previously generated human/GPT-4o codebooks, algorithmic code merging, and human contribution/grounding analysis.
evidence_records.Dataset name: Physics Lab community first-two-month discourse sampled around timestamp peaks
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 340 human codes; 652 machine codes overall; detailed analysis emphasizes 240 item and 282 verb-phrase codes
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: educational/community discourse, possibly involving youth; anonymization/consent not described here
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o-2024-05-13 for source outputs; robustness models/settings incompletely enumerated
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Research question, context, and role; no codebook/examples.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: alternative coding workflows plus algorithm/LLM merging; not agents
evidence_records.Agent roles: code generator, description generator, embedding/cluster merger, and contribution assessor
evidence_records.Human role: Four coders generate baseline codes; researchers assess merged-code grounding and contribution.
evidence_records.Generated outputs: open codes, merged code space, groundedness/broadness labels, unique coverage, and contribution categories
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Codes link to messages/examples; evaluators write analytical memos and counterexamples.
evidence_records.Baselines: four human coders with/without context and five machine workflows
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: Base generation appears once; appendix mentions six models, five temperatures, and five GPT-4o temperature-.5 repetitions “across 15 runs,” but arithmetic/design are unclear.
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: code counts, grounded/overbroad rates, unique coverage, contribution categories, and merge-agreement κ
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Groundedness/broadness review and blind evaluation of 81 sampled merged codes with contribution/grounding memos.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two main code evaluators plus author-team reconciliation
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Three-round κ .54, .67, .76; overall .68. Individual agreement with algorithm .78 and .56; one evaluator knew the algorithm.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive counts and κ; no inferential comparison
evidence_records.Principal results: Machine workflows were mostly grounded. Among 57 unique codes in 81 reviewed merged codes, 17 were human-only, 10 shared by both item methods, 10 item-only, 20 verb-only. Twenty made substantial contributions: eight human, two item, ten verb. Humans contributed more conversational dynamics; machines more content coverage.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: No IRB, consent, youth/community privacy, or governance statement.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Detailed arXiv paper; resources depend on prior/related papers; no standalone repository linked.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Single dataset/question, random subset of merged codes, and rapidly evolving models.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Subjective author-team contribution judgments; only 81/315 merged codes; evaluator familiarity; unclear robustness arithmetic; no participant/minority coverage analysis.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Dependent reuse of Prompts Matter corpus/codebooks; distinct contribution analysis, not independent dataset replication.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong plurality-aware evaluation: assess unique/substantial contributions, not only agreement; supports parallel co-coder designs and content-versus-conversational-dynamics coverage.

evidence_records.Full citation: Wei, Zheng, Yunqi Li, Yucheng He, Yuelu Li, Xian Xu, Huamin Qu, Pan Hui, and Muzhi Zhou. 2026. Unpacking Discourses on Childbirth and Parenthood in Popular Social Media Platforms Across China, Japan, and South Korea. Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media 20(1): 2466–2483. https://doi.org/10.1609/icwsm.v20i1.42761.
evidence_records.Title: Unpacking Discourses on Childbirth and Parenthood in Popular Social Media Platforms Across China, Japan, and South Korea
evidence_records.Authors: Zheng Wei; Yunqi Li; Yucheng He; Yuelu Li; Xian Xu; Huamin Qu; Pan Hui; Muzhi Zhou
evidence_records.Venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media 20(1): 2466–2483
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv:2510.06788v1 posted 2025-10-08 and marked accepted at ICWSM 2026; VOR published 2026-05-25. One family.
evidence_records.Research objective: Compare childbirth/parenthood discourse and stance across China, Japan, and South Korea.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: hybrid grounded theory and thematic analysis, topic modeling, sentiment classification, and regression
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: BERTopic/HDBSCAN clustering followed by human filtering/merging into literature-derived dimensions; hosted Qwen fixed sentiment; video metadata coding and regressions.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid, with induction constrained by five preselected dimensions
evidence_records.Domain: fertility, childbirth, parenthood, gender, and social-media discourse
evidence_records.Dataset name: Douyin China and TikTok Japan/Korea childbirth/parenthood corpus
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: public posts/comments; full data not released
evidence_records.Number of documents: 668 videos and 219,127 retained comments from 597,105 collected; China 105/74,828, Japan 317/82,887, Korea 246/61,412
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 219,127 retained comments; 68,974 comments/24% removed as off-topic after clustering
evidence_records.Language: Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean; originals preserved, cross-country theme alignment in English
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: fertility, gender/family attitudes, possible demographics, and Chinese provincial IP-geolocation metadata
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Paper says Tongyi Qianwen/Qwen 72B while repository calls hosted Qwen-turbo; embedding model, service snapshot, decoding, and most libraries not reported.
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Six sentiment-prompt refinement rounds on 1,000 comments/language; prompts include video stance/context, while repository passes but does not use title/source arguments.
evidence_records.Agent roles: cluster generator, human cluster/theme interpreter, and fixed sentiment labeler
evidence_records.Human role: One language-specific coder labels videos, senior reviews 10%; three coders merge clusters; senior family-studies scholar/team align themes; humans validate 1,000 sentiment cases/language.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: video, comment, topic cluster, and theme
evidence_records.Generated outputs: clusters, country themes, five dimensions, representative comments, sentiment labels, and regressions
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: One BERTopic representative document per theme plus topic-tree outputs; full quote/source coverage incomplete.
evidence_records.Baselines: human sentiment checks; RoBERTa mentioned as worse without comparative results; no topic-model baseline
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: none reported; stability asserted without repeated-run evidence
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: topic counts, κ for theme merging, sentiment accuracy/macro-F1, distributions, regression coefficients/p-values
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Video-code spot-check, independent cluster merging, and sentiment checks on 1,000 comments/country.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: one primary video coder/language plus senior checker; three theme coders; sentiment evaluator count/expertise not reported
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Average κ=.82 for theme merging; unit, per-country values, and calculation incomplete; no video/sentiment IRR.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: multinomial logit with year fixed effects; multiple-comparison control and clustered errors unclear
evidence_records.Principal results: Values dominated China (57.37%); Utility/Cost dominated Japan (34.51/27.01%) and Korea (51.27/16.00%). Anti/pro/neutral: China 50.12/19.98/29.54, Japan 30.03/28.66/41.05, Korea 31.16/32.88/35.57. Independent sentiment accuracy: China 88.4%, Japan 90.2%, Korea 97.7%.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Crawling: 10 hours/day for 15 days China and 19 days Japan/Korea; model compute/API cost not reported.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: VOR says published content only, usernames removed, photos/videos not saved, geolocation unlikely identifying, with no IRB/consent. Earlier arXiv’s “IRB XXXX” and claimed 10% sample release were removed—a material revision.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: https://github.com/YuchengHE-CHN/ICWSM-Unpacking-Discourses-on-Childbirth-and-Parenthood includes code/prompts/partial translated outputs, not full data. Code prints API key; only Chinese prompt hard-coded; label semantics conflict across files/paper.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Commenters not populations, demographics absent, coarse geolocation, and stochastic/language bias.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: 24% cluster removal may erase minority discourse; one coder/language; translation alignment; tuning/validation overfit; platform/period/algorithm confounds; stance-conditioned prompt leakage; nested comments treated independently.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Major multilingual hybrid case; require outlier-preserving evaluation, independent cross-language review, platform controls, source coverage, versioned prompts/models, clustered inference, and repository security checks.

quality_scores.Title: Qualitative Research in an Era of AI: A Pragmatic Approach to Data Analysis, Workflow, and Computation

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Longitudinal health corpus is appropriate to workflow guidance.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Computational pipeline is described but exact models/configurations are incomplete.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Manual/prior-work comparisons exist without a clean current baseline.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Ongoing team audit is strong but not a formal evaluation.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Prior F1 is relevant but provenance-separated poorly.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Disconfirming cases and reflexive interpretation are explicit.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Some prior reliability evidence, not a current controlled rerun study.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Teaching/code/templates are public; original data properly restricted.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims are generally cautious and methodologically proportionate.
